note.backdrop: Late in Friday's session the S&P 500 is down 0.4% and the Nasdaq 100 down 1.2% (they were down 0.8% and 1.7% at midday). It is a fall led by AI hardware, not a market-wide one: no market-wide move or fear flag, oil, gold and the dollar are flat, and the 10-year yield is up about one usual day's worth. The median chip stock is down 3.6%. Producer-price inflation came in cooler than expected and the market fell anyway, so the selling is not about interest rates. Bitcoin is down 3.3%, a little more than its usual day.

read.says: Truist cut Nvidia to Hold and its target to $174 from $346, saying the risks outweigh the valuation after the chief executive's resignation, including possible shipments to China; Craig-Hallum also cut it to Hold; William Blair and Oppenheimer upgraded AMD.

Bloomberg reported on Nov 12 that the Justice Department is investigating whether Super Micro servers were smuggled into China; Super Micro denies the reseller named was a customer; Dell fell 8% in the same session while Super Micro fell 3%.

Dell fell 8% as the AI server sell-off deepened after the Nvidia chief executive's resignation; it builds mostly around Nvidia hardware; its shares are down more than 35% in a month despite a $95 billion AI server backlog; it reports on Nov 24.

Rothschild & Co Redburn cut Broadcom to neutral and its target to $398 from $595, citing its reliance on OpenAI and Anthropic, which cannot yet pay their own way, and Broadcom's backstopping of customer financing.

singles.beneath: Modine was worth about $5.6 billion before the report, so the jump adds about $1.7 billion: the market is pricing a takeover premium with real odds of no deal, not an agreed price. Its partners are down 1% to 5% today, so this is read as one company's event, not a re-rating of data-center suppliers. A strategic buyer is paying up for AI data-center equipment in the same week the stock market is marking it down.
singles.cause: Samsung Electronics is in talks to buy Modine, a maker of data-center cooling systems, Bloomberg reported; no deal is final and talks could fail. The stock is up 29.7%.

singles.beneath: It closed on Thursday at $12.12, so $10 is a 17.5% discount: the fall is the stock moving to the price of its own share sale, not a judgment on anything new. The base deal is about 7% of its $2.1 billion market value, sold at that discount, by a company whose cash and equivalents covered under five quarters of its losses. Candel fell on the same day and the two have moved together for a year, but the causes are separate.
singles.cause: Vir priced a sale of 15 million new shares at $10 each, $150 million before an option for 2.25 million more. The stock is down 18.9%.

singles.beneath: Stifel now expects the launch in mid-2028. Candel's $203.1 million of cash funds it into the second quarter of 2028 by its own account, so the cash now runs out about when sales would begin. The delay turns a company funded to its launch into one that must raise money before it, which is what the new share-sale agreement is for. Canaccord cut its target to $13 from $25 and kept its buy rating, and the stock has recovered a third of its overnight fall.
singles.cause: Candel pushed the filing of its prostate-cancer drug application with the FDA from the fourth quarter of 2026 to mid-2027, and the same evening filed to sell up to $50 million of stock at the market. The stock is down 25.8%, after being down 39% overnight.

singles.beneath: Its three filed quarters of 2026 add up to $189.6 million ($52.6, $64.1 and $72.9 million), so the raised guidance implies a fourth quarter of $72.5-74.5 million: flat against the third quarter, after growth of 22% and 14% in the two quarters before. At about 22 times the last four quarters' revenue ($5.2 billion against $238.7 million), a stock priced for acceleration fell on guidance that says it stops. The fourth-quarter figure is my arithmetic from the guidance and the filed quarters, not a number the company gave.
singles.cause: Heartflow reported third-quarter revenue up 57% and raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $262-264 million from $246-250 million, and fell 17.1%. Management flagged a flat fourth-quarter pricing outlook on the call.

singles.beneath: $14 million of that revenue is a one-time payment. Without it revenue was about $55 million, up 21.6%, and most of the quarter's profit is the size of that one payment. The headline growth is more than twice the underlying growth.
singles.cause: Newsmax reported record quarterly revenue of $69.0 million, up 52.5%, net income of $15.2 million and an updated full-year outlook. The stock is up 27.1%.

singles.beneath: Guidance was reaffirmed and the stock still lost 8%, while its software partners are flat: the market is pricing the exit itself. No successor was ready, so the person who signs the numbers leaves before a replacement exists.
singles.cause: Commvault's chief financial officer is leaving for another company; the chief accounting officer becomes interim CFO on Dec 1 and a search firm has been hired. The company reaffirmed its guidance. The stock is down 8.1%.

singles.beneath: AI networking sells at lower margins and memory costs are rising, so more AI revenue means less profit per dollar of sales. That is a statement about the whole AI hardware business, not only Cisco: Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Arista fell with it.
singles.cause: Cisco reported record revenue of $18.5 billion, up 24%, and doubled its AI revenue outlook, and fell 6.3%: its non-GAAP gross margin dropped to 65.6% from 68.1% and its next-quarter revenue guidance is below the quarter just reported.

singles.beneath: The checks on Thursday found it 17% to 20% below Wednesday's close for most of the day after its results, yet Thursday's close was flat against the market: it rose back late that day. It is now back near where it traded through Thursday. Today's fall is that late rise reversing, not new information.
singles.cause: No filing and no story today; it is down 12.0% from Thursday's close.

singles.beneath: Tubeless pumps have been Insulet's ground, and Insulet is up 2.9% today, so the market is not reading the clearance as a threat to it. For Tandem it matters more than usual: it is losing money and carries $603.4 million of long-term debt against $72.8 million of cash and equivalents.
singles.cause: Tandem received FDA clearance for Tandem Mobi as a tubeless automated insulin pump with up to seven days of wear. The stock is up 15.1%.

singles.beneath: The other packaged-food companies it moves with are up about 2% today, so this is about bread and Flowers, not the food group. It had already fallen against the market in four of the five sessions before the report.
singles.cause: Flowers Foods missed on third-quarter earnings and sales (sales down 4.7%) and cut its full-year outlook on weaker bread volumes. The stock is down 8.6%.

themes.beneath: The two companies actually named in the scandal are falling least today: Nvidia -2.0% and Super Micro -1.2%, against 5% to 9% for the rivals and dependents. So Friday's selling is not about the scandal's direct damage. What is being marked down is the AI build-out as a trade, for three reasons that arrived in the same week. One: export-control enforcement is a risk to every seller of AI hardware, not to one. Two: the quality of AI revenue was questioned twice, by Cisco's results (record sales and a doubled AI outlook, but a gross margin 2.5 points lower on AI networking mix and memory costs) and by a downgrade of Broadcom that rests on customers that cannot yet pay their own way and on Broadcom backstopping their financing. Three: the stocks falling most are the ones that rose most and have the highest market betas (AMD 3.4), which is what an unwinding of crowded positions looks like. Nvidia now trades at about 13 times forward earnings after a 27% slide: the fear is priced less in Nvidia than in what depends on it.
themes.cause: Nvidia's chief executive resigned, effective immediately, on Thursday Nov 12, amid a scandal that includes reports of Nvidia chips diverted to China in breach of export controls. On Thursday money moved out of Nvidia and into its rivals. On Friday that reversed and the whole group was sold: AMD -9.0%, Dell -7.6%, CoreWeave -6.0%, Broadcom -5.1%, the median chip stock -3.6%.
themes.mechanism: Three routes. Rivals: AMD and Broadcom were bought on Thursday on the idea that Nvidia's customers would shift orders to them, so they had the most to give back; AMD had gained about 29% against the market in the five sessions before today. Dependents: Dell builds mostly around Nvidia hardware and CoreWeave rents out Nvidia chips, so doubt about Nvidia's leadership reaches their order outlook. The law: the Justice Department is reported to be investigating whether Super Micro servers reached China, so export-control enforcement now touches the server makers as well as the chip designer.

themes.beneath: The market's fall carries 1 to 2 points of each move. The other 6 to 8 points have no company cause: it is last week's gain being given back, the AMD pattern one size down.
themes.cause: None of the three has a filing or a story since the close. Each rose sharply in the past week against the market (Alpha & Omega +26.5% and +15.1% on Nov 6 and 9, Aeva +18.4% on Nov 6, Richardson +5.5% and +4.2%), each has a market beta of 2.7 to 3.9, and most of each one's partners (chips, lidar, quantum computing) are down 2% to 8% today.
themes.mechanism: They are held as part of the same AI and momentum trade as AMD. When that trade is cut, the high-beta recent winners are sold with it, whatever their own business news.

themes.watch: Whether they recover with the group. A filing from any of them would replace this explanation.
